page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, featuring 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 154 GB of local storage. The instance is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, as well as average throughput in large-block memory bandwidth tests. However, memory performance is constrained, with PassMark memory scores falling into the bottom 10% and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth ranking in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic operations are also limited, as evidenced by a poor PassMark CPU encryption test result, though the processor supports hardware-accelerated AES.

With its lower RAM-to-CPU ratio of 1:2, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for applications such as basic web serving, database operations, and lightweight multi-threaded tasks. However, it is less optimal for memory-intensive applications, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy cryptographic workloads due to its lower memory density and weak benchmark results in those specific areas.
